question: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the Hippocratic Oath and the Declaration of Geneva for Indian medical graduates?

answers.text: Indian graduates take the Hippocratic Oath at graduation, and the Declaration of Geneva is an optional international supplement.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Indian medical graduates do not take the Hippocratic Oath. The Declaration of Geneva-based oath is what is administered at Indian graduation ceremonies.

answers.text: The Declaration of Geneva (2017 WMA revision) is the modern ethical pledge administered at Indian medical graduation, replacing the Hippocratic tradition ceremonially.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The WMA Declaration of Geneva (last revised 2017) is the contemporary international medical pledge and is the basis for the oath administered at Indian MBBS graduation ceremonies.

answers.text: Both oaths are taken at graduation — the Hippocratic Oath for ethical commitments and the Declaration of Geneva for legal obligations.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Only one oath is administered at graduation. The Declaration of Geneva covers ethical obligations; there is no separate legal oath at graduation.

answers.text: Neither oath is taken by Indian graduates; the NMC Code of Ethics substitutes for an oath ceremony.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. A formal oath based on the Declaration of Geneva is administered at Indian graduation ceremonies as specified by the NMC.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: the Hippocratic Oath is foundational historically but is not taken by Indian graduates. The Declaration of Geneva (WMA, 2017 revision) is what is administered at Indian MBBS graduation.
Well done. The Declaration of Geneva (2017 revision) is the operative pledge — it is the modern successor to the Hippocratic tradition and the basis for the Indian graduation oath.
